summary: This PR adds a CSV export endpoint for invoices. The feature is wanted (linked issue #470 has maintainer sign-off) and the structure is clean, but the query builds SQL by string concatenation from a user-supplied filter, which is an injection path, and the export is never exercised end to end in the proof provided.
changeSummary: Adds GET /invoices/export.csv that streams the caller's invoices as CSV, filtered by an optional status query parameter.

productReview.userProblem: Finance users need to pull invoices into spreadsheets without copying from the UI.
productReview.rationale: Requested in #470, approved by the billing area owner in that thread. Scope matches the request; no extra options or defaults were introduced.

findings.title: SQL built by concatenating the status query parameter
findings.body: `status` comes straight from `request.args` and is interpolated into the WHERE clause. A request like `?status=paid' OR '1'='1` returns every tenant's invoices. Use a bound parameter; the ORM already supports `.filter(Invoice.status == status)`.

findings.title: CSV writer does not escape cells that start with =, +, -, @
findings.body: Invoice `memo` is user-entered text and is written verbatim. A memo of `=HYPERLINK(...)` executes as a formula when the export is opened in Excel. Prefix such cells with a single quote or use a library that does CSV-injection escaping.

findings.title: Export reads all rows into memory before streaming
findings.body: `rows = query.all()` materialises the full result set, so a tenant with 500k invoices will exhaust worker memory before the first byte is sent. `query.yield_per(1000)` keeps the streaming response actually streaming.

securityReview.summary: Two concrete injection paths in a new user-facing endpoint; both are fixable in this PR.

concerns.detail: SQL string concatenation from query parameter (see F1).
CSV formula injection via unescaped memo field (see F2).

testingReview.missingE2e: A request against the running service that downloads the CSV and opens cleanly, including one row with a comma and a quote in the memo.
lowValueTests: test_export_returns_200 asserts only the status code and would pass with an empty body.

rating.rationale: Useful feature with clear structure, held back by two injection defects and unit-only proof.

risks: The endpoint has no rate limit; a large tenant can trigger repeated full-table scans. Decide whether the existing per-route limiter should cover it before this ships.
praise: Tenant scoping is applied at the query root rather than filtered afterwards.
The route is documented in the OpenAPI spec in the same PR.
questions: Should `status` accept a comma-separated list, as the UI filter does?

inlineComments.body: Nit: `EXPORT_CHUNK` is defined but unused after the refactor in this PR.
